newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buy Nike puts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buy Nike puts.

text.p: Put buyers were out in force in Nike Inc options Wednesday as the stock fell after the company late Tuesday reported fiscal fourth quarter earnings that fell short of Wall Street expectations.
Among the options, the August 55 put traded 5,000 contracts, the July 55 put traded 4,155 and the July 60 put traded about 2,800.
"There are put buyers. Plenty of put buyers," said a market maker in the options. "A lot of customers are buying the August and July 55 puts."
In late trade, Nike shares were off 1-1/4 at 56-3/4.
Nike shares reached a session low of 55-5/8 before recovering. Consolidated turnover topped 4.7 million shares.
The market maker in Nike options said buyers and sellers were active in the July 60 puts.
The July 60 calls traded about 3,730 contracts.
"It's basically a lot of firms trading with each other," he said. "Market makers are kind of stepping aside. There's obviously two opinions."
Todd Salamone at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said some of the action appeared to show a mixed sentiment among investors.
"It looks like a big block went off at the bid, which suggests a possible put sell," he said. "That could be complacency with respect to how the shares are reacting to the news.
"But then there's some put buying," he added. "So it's just real mixed from a sentiment perspective."
The market maker said volatilities in the options was down slightly after the earnings news was out of the way and added that he was surprised by the amount of put buying.
"It's quite surprising the number of put buyers after a news release," he said. "Something's going on."
According to one options pricing model, implied volatilities in the Nike July options near the money ranged from the mid-30's to mid-40's.
In the August series, volatility was around 40.
On Tuesday, the footwear and apparel maker reported a 17 percent increase in fiscal fourth quarter profits, to $0.52 a share from $0.45 a share in the year earlier period.
The results were at the low end of the prediction the company issued May 29.
On Wednesday, Hambrecht & Quist cut its earnings estimates on Nike for the fiscal 1998 first quarter and full year.
